correctness.rationale: The pinned RESULT.md proof was reconstructed for every nonzero even integer p (including negative p), even m>2 and entry-point e>0. The doubling identity V_(2j)=V_j²−2(−1)^j gives ν₂(V_even)=1, and C_j=V_(2j+1)/p with C0=1,C1=p²+3,C_(j+1)=(p²+2)C_j−C_(j−1) proves ν₂(V_odd)=ν₂(|p|). If m=2^t r and t≥2, an entry V_e≡0 enforces e odd and 2^t|p. For odd r, gcd(V_f,V_(f+1))=2 makes V_(f+1) invertible, so the shifted sequence V_(f+n)=V_(f+1)U_n has precisely the U period d. For r>1, Cassini at d yields (−1)^d≡1 mod r, forcing d even. For t=1, π_U(2)=2 but π_V(2)=1, absorbed by even d since m>2; for t≥2, both periods mod 2^t are 2 by p≡0, and CRT/lcm yields equality. The r=1, m a 2-power case and p<0 are covered. Independent finite modular recurrence checks and V 2-adic checks corroborate but do not prove the infinite statement. The packaged verify.py was inspected and not treated as a proof; the external Lean/expert statuses remain not_performed.

evidence: Fiebig–Mbirika–Spilker Theorem 3.11 assumes discriminant p²+4 coprime to m; for p,m both even, gcd(p²+4,m)≥2.
Their Theorem 3.12 compares periods by a unit V_(e+1) modulo m; when both p,m even its unit hypothesis fails because consecutive V terms have gcd 2.
Corollary 3.13 explicitly covers p odd or p even/m odd, not p,m both even.
Renault 2013 full nine-page PDF studies generalized first-sequence periods, rank and order and the CRT behavior, not equality with the companion V period.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Relevant general equality theorems exclude the even-even hypothesis; the local valuation argument and Chinese-remainder reconciliation are not merely their special cases. In particular the modulus-2 discrepancy π_U(2)=2 versus π_V(2)=1 is absorbed by an even odd-part period or by sufficient p divisibility.

evidence: The prior shifted relation V_(f+n)=V_(f+1) U_n modulo r establishes period equality only where V_(f+1) is a unit; its unit criterion is invalid for an even modulus.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge original, exact resolution of the even-p/even-modulus q=-1 parity case left as Question 5.3 by Fiebig–Mbirika–Spilker. Directly inspected full arXiv HTML proves neighboring cases but not this one; its strongest unit and discriminant criteria fail at the even 2-primary factor. A full Renault primary PDF covers first-sequence periods/ranks rather than this companion equality. Semantic published-finding searches returned the indexed copy of the assigned claim itself (excluded as independent priority), and nearby unrelated Lucas results. Historical priority is qualified by older-notation and unindexed-literature risks, not asserted as absolute.

value.rationale: The theorem answers the specific natural parity gap Question 5.3 from a recent Lucas period/entry-point paper. Its exact all-index 2-adic valuation lemma explains the obstruction to the earlier unit argument, provides a reusable necessary divisibility criterion for V entry points, and fully settles the equality conditional for all even p,m>2. This is a mathematically motivated open classification, not a textbook substitution, tiny computational case or prior table reproduction.

limitations: The proof is conditional on the existence of e_V(m) and confined to q=-1; it does not settle q=1 or classify entry-point existence.
Direct finite recurrence checks are regression only and are not proof of the universal theorem.
